subject: Live packet emission SLA — carveout request from Praxis Health
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@praxishealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@praxishealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for live emission vs polled endpoint in SLA

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — Praxis engineering is excited about the transcription latency and the Redwood Optimize suggestions. We have a fast-fail safety requirement for our triage UI: the first partial transcription must be visible in under 300ms for short snippets, and sustained token rates need to support 40–60 tokens/sec when sessions are active.

Our procurement/legal team asked us to raise a formal exception to the standard streaming SLA language. The ask: allow a dedicated carveout for "live-packet emission" where time-to-first-packet (TTFP) is measured from session open to first non-empty chunk, and sustained rate is specified as a per-session median rather than absolute 99th percentile across multi-tenant pools. In return Praxis will commit to a reserved minimum throughput and a monthly reserved spend.

I attached a short draft with suggested wording and our network topology. Can we get Redwood's written position before we share this with our legal team next week?

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Lead Integrations, Praxis Health
attachments: Praxis_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (pdf), praxis-network-topology.png (png)

From: jonas.weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@praxishealth.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for live emission vs polled endpoint in SLA

Samira —

Appreciate the clarity and the draft. We can take an exception path but want to make sure expectations and operational guardrails are explicit. High-level response:

- We are open to a per-session median-based sustained-rate metric for dedicated reservations tied to a commit (monthly). We can't move our global 99th-percentile guarantees for our shared hosted endpoints; the carveout will be scoped to a Dedicated pool or a dedicated tenancy in Redwood Private.

- For the first-packet (TTFP) requirement: 300ms is aggressive but plausible on a colocated Dedicated pool with proper warm-up and K-V cache priming. We'll want a runbook to ensure connections are pinned and we can require client keepalive for session affinity.

- Operational conditions we foresee: pin-to-node routing, reserved capacity (minimum vGPU units), and a handshake / priming endpoint that Praxis uses to pre-warm KV caches for expected sessions. We can measure TTFP as you described, but the SLA will include an explicit exclusion for sessions that fail to follow the priming handshake or where Praxis network introduces >100ms RTT.

Next steps I propose: (1) our infra leads will propose binding wording for the carveout, (2) we share an SLI/SLO draft, and (3) Redwood legal will review the narrow amendment. Grace — can you drive the SLI language? Neha — can you coordinate with Legal on the carveout template?

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — jumping in with a first-pass SLI/SLO. I attached inline examples in the attached draft wording (see attached SLI table in the PDF). Key technical points:

- TTFP definition: time from authenticated session open (HTTP/2 or WebSocket upgrade complete) to first non-empty chunk byte on the application-level stream. We recommend measuring at the Redwood ingress edge for consistency.

- Exclusions: priming latency (requests tagged with x-prime: true), client-side inactivity, and network RTT > 100ms as measured by SYN/ACK latencies.

- Sustained rate: measured per-session as median tokens/sec across the session length; SLO target: >= 45 tokens/sec median for active sessions under committed capacity. Non-compliance in a month triggers remediation credits, not immediate termination.

- Monitoring & telemetry: Praxis must enable the session debug header we ship (x-rw-session-id) and share a sampling token so we can ingest traces. We'll include a joint dashboard for the dedicated pool with token-level breakdowns.

Samira — I'll iterate the SLI table into the legal amendment. Jonas — recommend adding the network diagram to the appendix.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Praxis — suggested redlines to Redwood carveout (SLA amendment)

Hi Jonas / Grace,

Attached are redlines to your suggested amendment. Our legal team's asks: include an objective measurement method for client-side versus server-side latency sources, limit exclusion windows to 90 days of rolling telemetry, and add language for an "operational remediation plan" that has escalation timelines.

Two specific items we want considered: (1) if Praxis hits >60 tokens/sec median for more than 5% of sessions in a month, we request a temporary increase path rather than immediate throttling; (2) require a quarterly architecture review where Redwood proposes quantization/ordering changes that might affect performance.

We attached the redlined PDF. Please advise whether Redwood can accept or propose alternatives.

Regards,
Praxis Contracts
attachments: Praxis_SLA_Draft_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: contracts@praxishealth.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: samira@praxishealth.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Praxis — suggested redlines to Redwood carveout (SLA amendment)

Thanks for the detailed redlines. Redwood Legal has reviewed the asks and here is our counter-proposal (summary):

- Measurement method: Agree to a deterministic attribution playbook. Server-side measurement will be Redwood ingress-edge timestamps and token emission logs; Praxis will provide client-side pings and we will compare. Discrepancies >50ms will default to the party that reported higher RTT unless evidence to the contrary is provided.

- Exclusion windows: we can accept telemetry retention limits (90 days) for the purposes of dispute resolution.

- High-burst path: Redwood can offer a temporary burst policy (72 hours, subject to reserved commit verification) when >60 tokens/sec median is observed; after that period we will require a short uplift commit or automated throttling. This gives Praxis breathing room.

- Quarterly architecture reviews: accepted. Redwood will provide performance impact statements with any recommended quantization or kernel changes and a 30-day notice prior to disruptive changes.

Attached: counter_draft_redwood_v1.pdf (will upload to the HubSpot deal). If that looks good we can route this to signature.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
